options: A plugin that translates HCL into calls against a specific API, such as Azure or AWS
A file format used only for variables
A synonym for a resource block
A tool for formatting .tf files
questions.explain: A provider is a plugin — one exists for Azure, AWS, and hundreds of other platforms — that translates your HCL into real API calls against that platform.

The local name, used only within this configuration
The real Azure storage account name
A required provider version
questions.explain: "images" is the local name — how this configuration's .tf files refer to the block. Azure never sees it; the real resource name comes from the name attribute inside the block.

questions.q: How does Terraform know to create a resource group before a storage account that belongs to it?
options: It always creates resource groups before any other resource type
The storage account block references the resource group's attributes, which establishes the dependency
The resources must be listed in that order in the file
A separate ordering file is required
questions.explain: Because the storage account block reads azurerm_resource_group.northbridge.name and .location, Terraform infers the resource group must be created first — no explicit ordering is written anywhere.

questions.q: What does the required_providers block, inside terraform { }, declare?
options: The variables a configuration accepts
Which provider(s) and version range the configuration needs
The output values a configuration produces
The local name of every resource
questions.explain: required_providers declares which provider plugins (like azurerm) and which version constraints the configuration depends on.

questions.q: What is the general reference pattern used to read another resource's attribute?
options: <attribute>.<type>.<local name>
<local name>.<type>.<attribute>
<type>.<local name>.<attribute>
$<type>:<attribute>
questions.explain: The reference pattern is always type, then local name, then attribute — for example azurerm_resource_group.northbridge.name.
